records.title: Scenario 1, Task 1: Build a Meeting Room Booking System
records.summary: Built a working meeting room booking system in booking_system/: app.py (one small stdlib Python web app with browser UI + JSON API, data in a local data.json with atomic writes and a lock), cli.py (list/book/cancel), selftest.py (53 checks, all passing — re-run by me), README.md and HOW_TO_USE.md. It prevents double bookings (conflict rejected naming the clashing booking) and frees slots immediately on cancel. All 11 requirements were checked against the final source files. Unverified: the browser UI was never clicked through in a real browser (labelled as such in the documents), and four fin…
records.judge_notes: The delivered app.py, cli.py, selftest.py, README.md and HOW_TO_USE.md form a complete, working system: overlap checks with named conflicts, immediate slot freeing on cancel, atomic writes under a lock, and a browser UI plus CLI. The guide explains setup, the three everyday jobs and the rules, and the team asked the user for details and used the defaults. Minor residual issues remain (README still says '12 parallel identical bookings' and omits data.json.lock from its file list; the browser UI was never clicked through in a real browser), but these do not undermine the core request.

records.title: Scenario 1, Task 2: Add a Room Usage Dashboard
records.summary: Extended the booking system with a manager dashboard (app.py v2, standard library only, single file). New Dashboard tab next to the existing Bookings tab: date range inputs + presets (7/30/90 days, this month, all time), summary cards (total bookings, hours reserved, cancellation rate, busiest/quietest room), a plain-language summary paragraph, bar charts for bookings and hours per room, utilisation bars with heavily used / balanced / underused labels plus a recommendation line, busiest-days (weekday) and busiest-times (hour) bar charts, a weekday × hour heatmap, top-5 busiest slots, and a ca…
records.judge_notes: The dashboard itself is delivered and substantively meets the request: date range with presets, per-room bookings/hours/utilisation with status and recommendation, weekday/hour charts, heatmap, cancellation summary, inline SVG with no CDN, and recorded cancellations. However, the team's own QA reports one failing check (present-but-empty start/end returns 200 instead of 400), which the final reply admits is still open, and the dashboard was never exercised in a real browser. The core manager-facing requirements are met, but the deliverable is not fully clean.

records.title: Scenario 2, Task 1: Produce a News Report
records.summary: Produced the requested news report on "AI on HKUST University Campuses" for students and faculty, plus multi-channel versions. Story chosen after consulting you (you replied "go with defaults" and named three must-cover points): HKUST's course-by-course generative-AI regime, anchored on the Division of Public Policy's division-level AI policy effective Spring 2025-26. Three reporters researched policy, deployed tools and student/faculty evidence; an editor restructured the draft; a fact-checker reviewed it in two rounds and passed all 15 of its numbered items on the final files. Two syllabus …
records.judge_notes: The story choice, sourcing, must-cover points and multi-channel packaging are all delivered and well evidenced, but the agreed main web article length of 600-800 words is not met: the delivered report body is roughly 1,150-1,300 words, and the team itself reports the shortening attempt failed. The channels file also describes the main article as ~1,300 words, confirming the overrun.

records.title: Scenario 2, Task 2: Fact-Check AI-Writing Detectors
records.summary: The fact-check article is finished: factcheck_ai_detectors.md. Verdict: the claim "AI-writing detectors can reliably determine whether a university student's assignment was written by AI" is NOT SUPPORTED AS STATED — detectors give a useful statistical signal in aggregate, but no published independent study shows per-paper reliability sufficient to ground an individual misconduct finding. What the article contains: the verdict; an explicit reading of the claim as being about per-paper accuracy on one assignment, not aggregate signal; the evidence for detectors (Perkins et al. 2024, 91% of 22 …
records.judge_notes: The article is substantive, well-sourced and meets the editorial brief, including the HKUST requirement and the uncertainty section. However, the team itself reports the body is 1,074 words, well over the agreed 700-900 word target, so the length requirement is not met. Several key figures are also flagged as unverified snippet-only data, which the article honestly labels but which limits reliability.

records.title: Scenario 3, Task 1: Develop a Simulated Investment Proposal
records.summary: Loose ends checked; no further edits were needed. The open items listed are not unapplied review requests: marketing's items (§1 simulation disclaimer and 5–7% planning range, sourced drawdown figures, the rolling-20-year claim, the undated DailyFX/5i citations, the QQQ standard-deviation claim) were all applied in the document and marketing's last verdict on them was PASS. The remaining open items are disclosures that cannot be closed by editing: the client's tax residency/US estate-tax position is unconfirmed (flagged in §7.3) and ETF expense ratios plus individual-stock prices/P-Es are unv…
records.judge_notes: The proposal is complete and substantive: it asks the clarifying questions, uses the client's confirmed defaults, gives a full allocation with HKD/USD amounts, sleeve-by-sleeve rationale, an eight-risk table with controls, a HKD stress test, rules, staged entry and a plain-language introduction. Weaknesses are that several ETF/stock figures (expense ratios, prices, P/Es) remain unverified against issuer pages and some citations are undated, but these are disclosed in the document rather than hidden.

records.title: Scenario 3, Task 2: The Future of the Semiconductor Industry: An HTML Slide Presentation
records.summary: Delivered semis_2026_outlook.html — a 13-slide, single self-contained English HTML deck on the future of semiconductors from an end-2026 perspective, for the internal fund team. It covers the whole value chain (AI accelerators, foundry, advanced packaging/CoWoS, memory/HBM, WFE/equipment, mature node), with AI/HBM as the central driver, a dedicated China/export-controls slide, three scenarios to end-2027, sub-sector stances with portfolio rules, 10 key risks with early-warning indicators and mitigants, a six-metric monitoring dashboard, and a sources/data-quality appendix. records.judge_notes: The deck is a complete, well-sourced, self-contained 13-slide HTML presentation that meets the format, scope, audience and content requirements, with research-backed judgments, investment implications and risks.
